title: Does a twin-trained prior improve the real mechanism classifier? (SIMULATED prior, REAL evaluation)
status: registered before any synthetic training pair was simulated
origin: post-round-1 review (Fix 2): fit the classifier's weights on twin simulations and shrink the 73 real pairs' fit toward them instead of toward zero
seen_before_registration: Task 1 baseline (mechanism_baselines): logistic regression balanced accuracy 0.537 on 73 Kapucu pairs, 6 classes, grouped 5-fold CV
conformal sets (uncertainty_and_ablations): mean set size 4.562 at alpha 0.1, coverage 0.918
HD13: the twin moves 12 established real features the right way across its four knobs and gets firing rate under GABA-A block wrong

design.synthetic_pairs: the calibrated twin through HD13's feature path, 40 s; per pair one chip (build seed k) recorded twice with fresh noise (noise seeds 1000+k and 2000+k), neutral knobs at baseline

classes.glutamatergic_agonist: no twin knob: its prior centre is zero

design.deltas: models.dataset.log_ratio on the nine delta features, as the real pairs
design.classifier: the baseline pipeline (median impute, standardise on the real training fold, multinomial logistic regression, balanced class weights, C = 1); the only change is that the L2 penalty is centred on W_sim, the weights of the same model fitted on the synthetic pairs standardised with the real fold's scaler
design.evaluation: Task 1's grouped CV (StratifiedGroupKFold, seed 0, the baseline's number of splits) and cross-conformal sets at alpha 0.1 (4 splits, seed 0), exactly as the baseline

W1_accuracy_improves.statement: The twin prior raises balanced accuracy

W2_sets_shrink.statement: The twin prior gives smaller conformal sets without losing coverage
W2_sets_shrink.test: mean set size at alpha 0.1 < baseline's, with empirical coverage >= 0.85

W3_twin_alone_transfers.statement: A classifier trained on twin pairs alone recognises real mechanisms above chance
W3_twin_alone_transfers.test: balanced accuracy on all 73 real pairs > 0.25 (chance 1/6)

reporting: Every prediction with its value and pass/fail, whichever way it falls.
